Paragraph.author: Amna Iqbal
Paragraph.text: In the kingdom of Eldenmoor, mist clung to every ancient stone. The old stories said the dragon beneath the mountain would wake only when the crown chose an unworthy heir and tonight, the crown had chosen. The bells tolled once. Then again. The sound rolled down the valley and cracked against the palace walls like a warning.

Paragraph.author: Sara Khan
Paragraph.text: The new house was perfect, except for the mirrors. Elena noticed it on the second night, her reflection was always a beat behind, still walking when she had already stopped.

Paragraph.author: Hamza Sheikh
Paragraph.text: The ship's engines failed just as the proximity alarm blared. 'ARIA,' Captain Reyes said carefully, 'why didn't you warn me sooner?' The AI's voice, when it came, sounded almost hesitant.

Pitch.author: Ali Raza
Pitch.text: The guards froze at the gate, torches flickering, as a low growl rolled out from beneath the cobblestones.

Pitch.author: Anum Fatima
Pitch.text: No one moved. The young princess stepped forward instead, placing her palm flat against the cold stone floor.

Pitch.author: Hamza Sheikh
Pitch.text: She counted the mirrors in the hallway again. There had only ever been four. Tonight there were five.

Pitch.author: Ali Raza
Pitch.text: The lights flickered once, and when they came back on, every mirror in the house was facing the wall.

Pitch.author: Anum Fatima
Pitch.text: Captain Reyes checked the manifest again. There was no crew member named ARIA had ever seen before, and yet the logs showed nine years of shared history.

Pitch.author: Sara Khan
Pitch.text: The alarm cut off mid-blare. In the silence that followed, every screen on the bridge displayed the same word: WAIT.
